CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right leg pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
The patient is a 43-year-old female who presented with right leg pain after a bowling injury. She was running up to the lane with her bowling ball when she swung it forward and struck her own right leg instead of the lane, causing her to fall. She reports minimal swelling but some bruising on the posterior aspect of the leg. She has limited ability to walk and describes the leg as very sore with ambulation. She states she would avoid stairs at all costs due to the pain. She has been alternating between ibuprofen and acetaminophen for pain management.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Atopic eczema. Previous surgical history of colectomy for diverticulosis complicated by diverticulitis.

MEDICATIONS
Fluocinonide as needed for eczema. Ibuprofen as needed. Acetaminophen as needed.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient bowls recreationally. Lives in home without stairs.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Significant tenderness to the lateral aspect of the right upper leg. No pain or tenderness with flexion or extension of the lower leg.

RESULTS
X-ray of femur: Normal. No evidence of fracture or swelling.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Contusion of right leg. Start Mobic 15 mg once daily as anti-inflammatory. Apply ice for pain management. Expect improvement within one week. Patient to return if not improving.
